Hi Olivia — thanks, and great context. I put together an initial packaging note and sizing assumptions (attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Tiers_Q2_2027.pdf). High level: we typically recommend starting with a small, memory-favored pool for stability and then add compute-heavy H100 instances if latency/throughput becomes the bottleneck. Below is a concise tradeoff and a starter commit you can use for procurement.

Quick perf / memory tradeoffs (rough, workload-dependent):
- L40S (48GB): Best perf/$ for small to medium sequence workloads where FP16 int8 kernels are sufficient. Good for high-throughput batched scoring. Lower memory than 80GB A100 so avoid for very long contexts. Estimated raw throughput: ~800-1,000 tokens/sec (512 tokens) on many quantized models.
- A100-40GB: Balanced memory and cost. Strong throughput for mid-size models; preferred if you have many concurrent smaller requests. Estimated: ~600-800 tokens/sec.
- A100-80GB: Use when KV cache pressure or model memory requires it (long context or bigger model variants). Also simplifies multi-model hosting. Estimated throughput similar to A100-40 for same model family but enables larger batch sizes.
- H100-80GB: Highest single-request latency performance and best perf/latency for large model families; higher perf/$ for low-latency needs but higher unit cost. Estimated throughput: ~1,200-1,600 tokens/sec (depends on kernels/quant).

Sizing rule-of-thumb for 50 sustained QPS @ 512 tokens: tokens/sec demand = 50 * 512 = 25,600 tokens/sec (sustained).
- Conservative pool sizing (with 2x headroom for spikes and background jobs): target ~50k tokens/sec effective capacity.
- Example pool builds (effective capacity approximations):
  * 4 x H100-80 (1,200-1,600 t/s each) -> ~5k t/s nominal -> with batching ~20-24k t/s; require 4-6 nodes depending on model mix and tail latency targets.
  * 6 x A100-80 -> ~600-800 t/s each -> ~3.6k-4.8k t/s; need 10-12 nodes to hit the same headroom.
  * 8 x L40S -> ~800-1,000 t/s each -> ~6.4k-8k t/s; need 6-8 nodes depending on batching.

Pricing (ballpark, committed pool monthly list price per GPU unit):
- L40S-48GB: $3,600 / GPU / month
- A100-40GB: $4,800 / GPU / month
- A100-80GB: $6,400 / GPU / month
- H100-80GB: $9,200 / GPU / month

Discount guidance by commit term / volume (examples):
- 3-month commit: 8-12% off list
- 6-month commit: 15-18% off list
- 12-month commit: 20-28% off list (higher volumes tier into 25-35%)

Recommended starter commit for Neptune (low-friction):
- 6-month committed pool, mixed fleet: 4 x H100 + 4 x L40S (mix to support batch scoring + low-latency paths).
- Target committed units: 8 GPUs (we can make a minimum exception for Neptune)
- Estimated committed monthly list: (4*9,200) + (4*3,600) = $36,800 + $14,400 = $51,200 / month before discount.
- With a 18% 6-month commit discount -> $41,984 / month.

SLA & addenda: standard 99.9% regional availability for Dedicated pools; 99.95% SLA available as a paid add-on with reserved capacity and priority routing. We'll attach our SLA addendum and SOC2 pack.

Next steps: if that starter mix looks reasonable, I can loop in pricing (Marissa) to firm numbers and generate a formal quote and DocuSign bundle. Also attach a workbook if you'd like us to run a more exact throughput run using a representative model.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Tiers_Q2_2027.pdf

Subject: Neptune pricing ask — discount flexibility (deal NEP-2027-013)

Team — procurement asked if we can do a 4 GPU minimum and a 6-month commit; their target is the mixed starter pool (4 H100 + 4 L40S) but procurement wants a smaller entry point to start. Notes and ask:

- Proposal options I want us to consider:
  Option A (Aggressive acquisition): 12-month commit, 8 GPUs (mix), 25% off list, 24/7 premium support included, 99.95% SLA (adds $1k/mo normally but waive for 12m).
  Option B (Practical starter): 6-month commit, 4 GPUs committed (we will reserve a minimum of 2 H100 + 2 L40S), 18% off list, include SOC2 pack and 6-week canary rollout plan.
  Option C (Low-friction): 3-month commit, 4 GPUs, 12% off list, no premium SLA by default, option to upgrade.

- Financial impact: Option B would be ~ $41,984 / mo list*0.82 = ~$34,447 for the 8-GPU mix; with their ask to commit only 4 GPUs we'll need a restructure — we can show a staged commit (start 4 GPUs committed / 4 GPUs on a short-term burst/reversible pool with higher overage pricing).

- Exceptions: procurement wants minimum of 4. Our standard minimum is 8 for mixed fleets (economics/placement), so this requires a sales exception. I recommend approving Option B for this account with a required review after 3 months and a 30-day expansion notice clause.

Can Marissa and Ben sign off on giving them the 6-month/18% path and the reduced min to 4 GPUs (with the staged commit wording)? Karthik — are there infra constraints I'm missing for allowing a 4 GPU min for a mixed H100+L40S pool in US-EAST?

Thanks,
Hannah

- 6-month committed contract; pricing at 18% off list for the committed 4 GPUs (2 H100 + 2 L40S).

- Include SLA addendum (attached) and SOC2 artifacts.
